 A best IIT resume must have key qualifications and competencies categorized well into sections. Headlines may be like academic qualifications, scholastic achievements, internship and research projects, technical skills, work experience, extracurricular etc. Do not overload your resume by accommodating more information. Know that simple things gain more attention. So, format your resume accordingly.
 2. Length of a resume
 It is okay if your resume is somewhat lengthy. Keeping things simple has nothing to do with having a 3-page resume. Just make sure that you do not describe a particular topic too much. If you have more experience working as an IITian or many essential skills that you cannot skip, then it is better to mention those points. The ideal number of pages of a resume should not exceed 2 pages but again, it varies from individual to individual.
 3. Strategy to hide weak areas
 It is quite acceptable that you may have certain weak points in your resume. Disguising them is your task. You must present your resume in such a manner that only highlights your expertise and draws less attention to your weak spaces. Let's say, you have a poor GPA in a particular educational qualification, you can leave that part and instead display your activities, papers, awards etc. Alternatively, you can talk about your major GPA that may get the interviewer to overlook other minor GPAs.
 4. Use some colours
 Using some colours like green or blue to get the headlines noticeable is one criterion of a good resume. This same rule also applies to IITians. Since there may be a lot of qualifications, achievements and awards, it becomes necessary to look out for ways that can grab attention. Using colours and different fonts will certainly make the resume appealing. However, do not use too many colours as you don't want to create a rainbow out of a resume. Other than white for the background, the secondary colour should be black and for emphasis, you can use blue or green. Also, use bold fonts where needed. Italics are also fine to break away from the monotonous font that is generally used.
 5. Other interests
 You may choose to add to the "Other interests" section of your resume where you will be highlighting your hobbies or other recreational activities. The housing has an inlet and an outlet, and the incoming steam flows through the inlet and into the bucket. As the steam flows through the bucket, it cools and condenses, and the condensed steam collects in the bottom of the bucket.

The weight of the condensed steam causes the bucket to invert, and the steam is trapped in the inverted bucket. The condensed steam is then drained from the trap through the outlet.

prompt: Why do you need to use command prompt?
text:
There are a number of good end-user solutions using GUIs that lie between pure text command lines and highly graphical programming.
 With respect to graphical programming, it’s important to note that Ivan Sutherland’s Sketchpad — my vote for the first real interactive graphics system (1962) — was programmed graphically (in terms of telling the system to “figure out how to make this happen” — using constraints).
Ivan Sutherland making a bridge simulation from scratch by drawing and programming with constraints.
 Ivan’s older brother Bert — after getting out of the Navy — did a PhD thesis (ca 1965) called “Online Graphical Specification of Procedures”, which was my vote for the first data flow and “wired up” components graphical programming system.
A graphical program for square root that creates a new component (in the upper left quadrant) using connectable dataflow programming.
 Just a little later (ca 1968) a very usable flowchart programming system — GRAphical Input Language (GRAIL) — was done at RAND by Tom Ellis et al.
This system was capable of larger scale programming as well as simple programming for end-users (which might be a single screen-full of wired up things to do). Each element can be tapped on to reveal its programmed meaning, also in terms of flow diagrams. This allowed them to program the entire GRAIL system in itself. For debugging, the diagrams can be run slowly (there was a speed control) and would show the actions through the diagrams step by step.
 Another constraint system that followed in the footsteps of Sketchpad, was ThingLab by Alan Borning (ca 1977) done in Smalltalk at Parc.
 Another early dataflow system was Fabrik, done by Dan Ingalls et al. in Smalltalk in the early 80s.
 An exemplary system at “industrial strength” was the graphical dataflow system “MetaFour” done in the late 80s by Parc alums Dave Liddle, Yogen Dalal, et al. which was used heavily for a number of years by large companies — e.g. Proctor and Gamble — initially for “data mining”, and then for many other applications. The end-users graphically connected “data sources” (represented as a “node”) to “data filters” and “data massagers” (also represented as nodes). The system was supplied with a large repertoire of useful nodes — some of which allowed further programming in various ways, including the ability to encapsulate a whole dataflow diagram system. This system was nicely matched to the end-users and was supplied with large CRTs that provided enough real-estate for the graphical programs.
 As with all programming systems, graphical programming is generally much easier to write than to read. Because there is less directionality in 2D or more D, reading can be extremely difficult (like reading electronic circuit diagrams).
 Alan Borning’s ThingLab solved part of this problem by allowing dual mode operation: generally one programmed by graphical building, and a visitor would understand by moving back and forth between the construction and a textual rendering that was more narrative-like. This was a good solution.
 The MetaFour system’s solution was also a very good one in that the problem domain and how it was handled plus the available hardware, display, etc., were all well matched up.
 The advent of wide angle VR could make a big difference. Graphical programming requires more real estate, and is much more effective with larger viewing angles (this is also true for good UIs for textual programming, just more so). My guess is that an attempt at a new system today by really good designers and programmmers who are willing to do the extra UI work needed (these are in very short supply these days), could produce quite a breakthrough in “more-intuitive programming”.
 However, programming is not the same as good design — either for functionality or appearance — so at some point computerists really need to buckle down to learn how to do good systems design regardless of the means of programming …

prompt: What coins were in use in Italy in the 6th century A.D. and what was their value?
text:
There were actually three competing sets of coinage (four, if you count the huge number of older issues that were still in use) at different points in the 6th century. This wasn’t much of a problem, since ancient coins were almost always valued for their metal content and not their face value. But the coinage actually throws an interesting light on the strange state of sixth century Italy.
 Italy was half-Roman borderland, no longer the heart of the empire. It was ruled by the [LINKED_TEXT: Ostrogothic Kingdom] [URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ostrogothic_Kingdom], which emerged after the imperial succession ended in the west in 476. However, the Roman cast of Italian life remained strong. In theory, the Ostrogoths were imperial subjects, allowed to operate their own ‘kingdoms’ in return for military service to the emperor. In practice, however, the Ostrogoths were an independent power ruling over a Roman citizenry — sometimes amicably, and sometimes not.
 The ambiguous relationship is reflected in the coinage. Ostrogothic coins were clearly modeled on Roman ones. This is a [LINKED_TEXT: solidus] [URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solidus_(coin)] of Ostrogothic king [LINKED_TEXT: Theoderic] [URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theoderic_the_Great] I, aka. “the Great”.
The inscription reads D N ANASTASIVS P F AVG, “Our lord Anastasius, Dutiful and blessed emperor” on the front and “VICTORIA AUGGG” , “Victory of the emperors” on the back. Theoderic ended up in Italy at the invitation of emperor [LINKED_TEXT: Zeno] [URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeno_(emperor)], Anastasius’ predecessor who decided that Theoderic in Italy could help defeat a different Germanic king, [LINKED_TEXT: Odoacer] [URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odoacer] — and that Theoderic was less of a threat in Italy than he had been in the Balkans.
 That solidus was the reference unit for sixth century money, like the dollar today. However it was worth much more: it was about 3.25 grams of gold (roughly $125 at today’s gold prices ). Most ordinary people rarely saw one: a single solidus would pay a soldier’s salary for six months or so, or buy a couple of pigs, or maybe 8 bushels of wheat.* There were also smaller gold coins, [LINKED_TEXT: tremisses] [URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tremissis] or ‘thirds’ which were 1/3 of a solidus — perhaps not everyday coinage for ordinary folk, but more likely to be seen in the market.
 Most day-to-day coins were variants on the [LINKED_TEXT: nummus, ] [URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nummus]a tiny bronze coin which was supposed to be 1/7200th of a solidus — a trifle over 1/100th of a cent today. A loaf of bread probably cost around 20 or 30 nummi; a liter of wine maybe 15.
 Because a single nummus was as impractically small as a solidus was impractically large, a number of denominations were introduced in the early sixth century to make things easier. Here’s a 5-nummi coin (note the large roman numeral on the reverse) from Theodoric’s son Althalaric.
A very common denomination was the [LINKED_TEXT: follis] [URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Follis], worth 40 nummi. The follis was done in bronze and was about half an inch or 13 mm in diameter. This example is from the Gothic king [LINKED_TEXT: Theodahad] [URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodahad]. prompt: What is the good enough mother theory ?
text:
The "good enough mother" theory is a concept introduced by the British pediatrician and psychoanalyst Donald Winnicott in the 1950s. It emphasizes the importance of a mother (or primary caregiver) being able to meet the physical and emotional needs of a child without striving for perfection. According to Winnicott, being a "good enough mother" means providing an environment where a child can grow and develop while still experiencing some frustrations and challenges. These experiences help the child develop resilience, independence, and the ability to cope with life's difficulties.

The theory suggests that trying to be a perfect parent can actually be harmful to a child's development, as it may hinder their ability to learn from mistakes, develop problem-solving skills, and build a sense of self. Instead, the "good enough mother" offers love, support, and care, while allowing the child to gradually develop their own sense of autonomy and independence. This approach encourages a more balanced and adaptive relationship between the parent and child, fostering healthy emotional development.

Conway's Game of Life is a mathematical model of a cellular automaton, developed by the British mathematician John Horton Conway in 1970. It is a "zero-player game," meaning that its evolution is determined by its initial state and requires no further input.

The game consists of a grid of cells, each of which can be either "alive" or "dead." The evolution of the game is determined by the following rules:

1. Any live cell with fewer than two live neighbors dies, as if by underpopulation.
2. Any live cell with two or three live neighbors lives on to the next generation.
3. Any live cell with more than three live neighbors dies, as if by overpopulation.
4. Any dead cell with exactly three live neighbors becomes a live cell, as if by reproduction.

These rules are applied simultaneously to all cells in the grid in each iteration, resulting in the birth, death, and survival of cells. The patterns that emerge can be highly complex and unpredictable, and have been the subject of much study and fascination.

Conway's Game of Life has applications in various fields, including computer science, physics, and biology. It is also a popular topic in recreational mathematics and has inspired numerous artistic and visual representations.

text:
([LINKED_TEXT: CLICK HERE] [URL: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1yHibUorM-O-hb4e17Z2lPPCEm-FB4are/view?usp=drivesdk] to get your free dog training guide)
 I think many answers are missing the point entirely. At least from what I assume the question is asking - why are there (naturally occurring) big cats and no (naturally occurring) big dogs.
 In the same ecosystem with the same prey animals, there will always be larger cats than dogs.
 First off we need to remember that hominins have caused a mass extinction event within the last 500,000 years and there were a lot more large animals than there are today.
 So we can extend our list of big cats and big dogs to include sabre-toothed cats which were far bigger than the panthera line of big cats; large panthera big cats such as cave lions which were quite a bit larger than the Siberian Tiger; and large dogs such as the dire wolf.
 This is possibly the largest dog, Epicyon. It is earlier than the canid wolves we are familiar with today with a shorter muzzle. Though its not a grey wolf in the picture, a grey wolf is almost the exact same size as the smaller dog in that picture.
 Some lion species were perhaps 50% larger than the African lion (so another half a lion added to a lion).
 And the largest sabre-toothed cats were even heavier for their size, as they had heavily muscled bodies designed for wrestling massive prey, rather than lighter bodies of lions and tigers designed to manipulate prey until they can get a bite.
 So both cats and dogs have been much larger than they are today. The thing to remember is the places with the largest animals also tended to have the largest human populations which wiped out the large animals- the verdant forests of Europe, Asia and America have been almost wiped clean of large wildlife whereas dry places like Africa have had most of their wildlife left intact. Africa is seen today as a hotspot for large animals but in actuality it doesn’t have many large animals, which is why it is so intact today. Compared to extinct lions, extinct hyenas, extinct rhinos, extinct mammoths and mastodon et cetera, the African animals we think of as large today are by no means the largest - Africa wasn’t a great place for large animals on the whole.
 The fact remains, though, that any environment that has had a dog (basically every habitat in the last 10 million years) has had a significantly larger cat.
 For an identical habitat with identical prey animals, cats are bigger than dogs.
 As for why, it is all down to hunting style.
 Wolves today kill some of the largest animals in their habitats- musk ox, bison, the largest deer- are all prey to wolves. Similarly wild dogs and hyenas can kill prey many times their size.
 For a cat to kill something so large, it has to be far more powerful and muscular than a dog does.
 Predators will evolve to kill all prey in the environment. This means even the largest animals will have a predator except for the very largest (mammoths, elephants and indricotheres) which require the predators to become far too massive and specialised, hugely reducing the prey they can take.
 So cats and dogs will both grow to the size required to take down the largest (except for the super large) prey in the environment. Dogs hunt larger animals by endurance, pack intelligence, and by nipping and biting to wear an animal out in the chase. Cats hunt larger animals by wrestling and grappling.
 For dogs the size needed to kill a large prey animal can be much, much smaller than it can for cats.
 This is why cats are, and in the past have been, bigger than dogs.

Title: Asymmetric Encryption in Accounting: Enhancing Data Security and Trust in Financial Transactions

Abstract:

The rapid growth of digital technology and globalization has transformed the accounting industry, leading to increased demand for effective and secure mechanisms to safeguard sensitive financial information. Asymmetric encryption, also known as public key cryptography, has emerged as a critical solution for ensuring data security and trust in financial transactions, particularly in the realm of accounting. This study explores the application, benefits, and challenges of implementing asymmetric encryption in accounting, with the aim of providing a comprehensive understanding of its impact on the industry and offering recommendations for its adoption.

Asymmetric encryption relies on the use of a pair of keys – a public key for encryption and a private key for decryption – ensuring that only the intended recipient can access the encrypted data. This method has been widely adopted in various industries, and its application in accounting has the potential to revolutionize the way financial information is transmitted, stored, and accessed. The incorporation of asymmetric encryption in accounting systems can significantly enhance the security of sensitive data, reduce the risk of unauthorized access, and improve overall confidence in the accuracy and integrity of financial records.

One of the primary benefits of asymmetric encryption in accounting is the elimination of the need to share a single key for both encryption and decryption processes. This reduces the risk of key compromise, as the private key remains securely with its owner, preventing unauthorized access to confidential financial data. Additionally, asymmetric encryption enables secure communication between multiple parties, facilitating seamless collaboration and data sharing among accountants, auditors, and clients.

Furthermore, asymmetric encryption can be integrated with other advanced security technologies, such as blockchain and digital signatures, to create a robust and comprehensive security framework for accounting systems. This integration can effectively mitigate risks associated with data breaches, fraud, and cyberattacks, ensuring the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of financial information in the digital age.

However, the implementation of asymmetric encryption in accounting also presents several challenges. These include the complexities associated with key management, the need for continuous updates and maintenance of cryptographic algorithms, and the potential for increased computational overhead. To overcome these challenges, it is essential for accounting professionals and organizations to invest in appropriate training, infrastructure, and support systems.

In conclusion, the adoption of asymmetric encryption in accounting has the potential to significantly enhance the security and trustworthiness of financial transactions in an increasingly digitalized and interconnected world. By understanding its benefits and addressing its challenges, accounting professionals can leverage this technology to safeguard sensitive financial data and strengthen the overall integrity of the industry. Further research and collaboration between academia, industry, and regulatory bodies are essential to facilitate the widespread adoption of asymmetric encryption and ensure its effective integration into accounting practices.

prompt: What is the weirdest object you've ever found?
text:
In 1968 I found an un-fired 20mm anti-aircraft shell buried in a dirt road behind my aunt’s house outside of Boston. In this picture the 20mm round is the one on the left (50 caliber on the right).
So I was maybe seven or eight years old and as children we often walked up to our aunt’s house a few blocks away. Behind her house was an unpaved road that was poorly maintained by the city. I think the residents liked it that way because it kept traffic off and when there was traffic it had to go slowly because of all the massive rain holes and pot holes. In those days the city would fill the road with gravel and cinder ash from the incinerators, and for decades before, filled it with clinker ash from the steam trains. People dumped their coal stove ash in the pot holes as well, in order to fill them. The rains would turn the ash into a sort of cake or concretion and it was better than relying on the city of Boston, which in those days was not paying much attention to the outside environs of Readville much then or in the years before. As children we often splashed through the ashy-muddy puddles to the disgust of our mother.
 But this one day it was dry as dust, the sun baking the road. We were rambling home from having tea and shoveling coal at my grandmother’s house (she could only cook via a coal stove). As we walked home I noticed something sticking out of a particularly deep dried-up puddle and I pulled it out. It looked like a big bullet. It was very old, rusty and the tip was lose enough to revolve completely around the shell casing. I brought it home.
 That night at dinner I showed it to my family. When my dad saw it, he leapt up from his chair as if he had been struck with a cattle prod, his newspaper falling to the floor in pieces. Everyone was surprised. My father never moved quickly. He grabbed the shell from my hand, ran to the back door and winged it into the yard. Then he turned on me, his eyes burning.
 “Where did you get that?,” he yelled at me. I might have wet myself. My father was never a man you wanted to get angry. I sank into the chair. All my brothers and sisters were staring at me, their forks halfway to their mouths, forgotten.
 “Where did you get that,” he demanded again. My mother put her hand on my head to comfort me.
 “I found it in a puddle on Lakeview Place near the Kunkle’s house,” I stammered.
 “Don’t you touch it,” he warned, “I’ll get rid of it after dinner.”
 And he sat down and picked up his paper. What was it, I thought. Everyone was asking.
 “It’s a bomb,” my dad said. In my childlike mind I didn’t see how that rusty, pitted ancient thing could be any danger to anyone. It just looked cool, like a big bullet or a rocket ship. But my dad was insistent, “It doesn’t matter how old those things are. They can go off at any time. Don’t ever touch things like that.”
 How did a 2omm anti-aircraft round get into a puddle in Readville, MA? One can only speculate. Maybe some veteran brought it home from the war; maybe some guy in a local AA unit in Boston took one as a souvenir. Maybe it fell from an ash bucket when he disposed of it and was buried in the dirt. It had been there for quite some time, in the rain, snow, heat of summer, run over by cars and vehicles and yet there it sat, year after year waiting for me to find it.
 I never saw it again. My dad took it, what he did with it I don’t know. He had been in the war, still had screaming nightmares from years of combat and he certainly knew what the thing was. But we never spoke of it again, and yet in all these years I have never forgotten finding the curious thing or my dad’s lightning reflexes when he saw me bring it up from the floor for dinner-time show-and-tell.

text:
There are several potential societal and economic implications of the centralization of AI technology:

1. Concentration of power. If a few large companies control the development and application of advanced AI, it could lead to a concentration of power and influence. These companies could dominate entire sectors of the economy and society. There are concerns about "algorithmic monopolies" where a single company's AI system becomes the dominant platform. This could negatively impact competition and innovation.

2. Bias and unfairness. If the teams building AI systems are not diverse and inclusive, it could lead to AI technologies that reflect and amplify the biases of their creators. This could have major negative impacts on marginalized groups. Centralized control of AI could make it harder for outside groups to scrutinize and audit AI systems for problems like bias. 

3. Job disruption. Advanced AI deployed by large tech companies could significantly disrupt labor markets and the economy. While AI may create new types of jobs, it is likely to eliminate some existing jobs, especially those involving routine, repetitive tasks. This could exacerbate economic inequality. Retraining and transitioning workers to new types of jobs would require a coordinated societal effort.

4. Lack of transparency and accountability. If people do not understand how centralized AI systems work and make decisions, it will be difficult to hold the systems and their creators accountable. Bias or errors in the data or algorithms powering the AI could negatively impact individuals without clear mechanisms of redress. This could undermine trust in AI and in the institutions that deploy it.

5. Cybersecurity risks. Large, centralized AI systems are an attractive target for cyberattacks and hacking. If compromised, they could be manipulated for malicious ends like fraud, manipulation, or disruption. This could have major societal consequences, especially if critical infrastructure relies on these AI technologies. Ensuring the security and integrity of AI systems is crucial.

In summary, the centralization of AI in a few large companies poses risks around concentration of power, bias, job disruption, lack of transparency, and cybersecurity. prompt: Do vocal exercises really help your singing become better?
text:
Vocal exercises are an important part of a singer's training. Singers benefit from daily vocal exercises in many ways. All voice lessons begin with vocal exercises for good reason.
 Singing voices emanate from the lungs with the flow of air being controlled by the diaphragm. The air travels through the vocal cords into the mouth over the tongue and teeth and finally through the lips. All of these parts of our bodies are muscles with the exception of the teeth. To control the sound produced so it is on pitch, in rhythm, and enunciated clearly, singers must learn and practice controlling all of these muscles. Vocal cords must gain strength in order to be able to produce musical notes accurately for the required length of time. Additionally, singers must develop lung capacity to be able to complete long musical phrases, reach high notes with ease, and produce enough volume to be heard.
 The first exercises are to warm up the voice. These can vary. A couple of examples include the syllables "ma, mae, me, mo, moo" on a single pitch and then working either up or down the scale repeating the process or humming a simple note pattern. You are more likely to be able to match and maintain a pitch properly when humming. Humming causes the throat to widen, the soft palate to lift, and the nasal passages to open. All of these are desirable for singing. The single pitch with alternate vowel sounds starting with an "m" sound is another exercise which places all the parts of your anatomy in their proper positions for singing.
 Other exercises will work on different aspects of singing. Production of clear vowel sounds is extremely important when singing. In almost all cases, you will hold the vowel sounds. The consonants are brief sounds on either side of the vowel. Expect to spend the majority of your exercise time on varying progressions of vowel sounds. Lip and tongue placement can be especially important for clarifying the vowel sound and staying on pitch. For instance, the "ee" sound can easily become sharp in pitch if the mouth shape is too broad.
 Some exercises are designed to work your diaphragm and make it stronger. An example is "Ding, ding, ding" worked as staccato notes in a descending scale. Put your hand on your abdomen just at the bottom of your ribcage. You should feel a bounce here as you control the flow of air with your diaphragm.
 Another group of exercises work through your natural break point between your chest voice and your head voice. This group of exercises is designed to smooth the transition between the full, powerful chest voice and the lighter head voice. An example of this type of exercise is the octave slide either up or down through the scale. Once you've completed a full slide progression based on one note, move up a half step and repeat.
 Being heard is the goal of singing so there are some exercises designed to help singers project their voices to the balcony seats without injuring their voices. To project a voice is not about volume control which will be addressed next. Voice projection is about sending a voice through space such that a listener can hear it clearly and distinctly. Singing "Yah, Yah, Yah, Oooo" in a descending scale or yodeling are examples of ways to practice voice projection.
 Volume control while maintaining pitch is another feature that vocal exercises aim to develop. Holding a vowel sound on a pitch while gradually increasing and then gradually decreasing the volume is an example of this type of exercise.
 Accurate jumps between pitch intervals is the goal of exercises which involve pitch changes of any interval size. In addition to the exercises which walk the voice up and down the scale, there are exercises which have the voice transition by other intervals; thirds, fifths, and octaves are common.
 Another class of exercises works on agility of lip, tongue, and soft palate motion. Let's face it, some songs are fast and the words have to tumble out distinctly. The only way to do that is to be able to move the mouth through the required shapes swiftly.
 All of the exercises listed above help you develop pitch matching and train your ear to hear your voice and accompanying instrument(s). Your body will learn how it feels to produce the sound properly and when you perform, the muscle memory that you have built through the exercises will carry over. A quick note on performance, it is very common for singers to become sharp when they perform. This is because your whole body tightens up including your throat muscles and vocal cords. Tightening produces a sharper pitch. Practice stress reduction techniques and do these within the hour before the performance to reduce the anxiety level.
 Finally, singing depends on lung capacity. You need tremendous amounts of air to produce the notes in a musical phrase. While daily singing practice will increase your lung capacity, serious singers should also incorporate regular aerobic exercise into their routines. Find an activity you enjoy that makes you breathe hard - running, brisk walking, swimming, aerobics, dance - any of these will have a positive impact on your singing ability.

prompt: Write a recursive query in SQL for postgres.
text:
Here's an example of a recursive query in SQL for Postgres:
```sql
WITH RECURSIVE category_tree AS (
  SELECT category_id, name, parent_id, 1 AS depth
  FROM categories
  WHERE parent_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT c.category_id, c.name, c.parent_id, ct.depth + 1
  FROM category_tree ct
  JOIN categories c ON c.parent_id = ct.category_id
)
SELECT depth, name
FROM category_tree
ORDER BY depth, name;
```
This query defines a common table expression (CTE) called `category_tree` that recursively expands a list of categories and their parents, starting from the top-level categories with no parent. The CTE uses a `UNION ALL` to combine two parts of the query:

1. The first part selects the top-level categories and their depth (starting at 1).
2. The second part joins the `category_tree` CTE to the `categories` table using the `parent_id` column, and recursively adds the current category's children to the CTE.

The final query selects the depth and name of each category, ordered by depth and name.

prompt: What are the steps in writing a dissertation?
text:
Be sure to take Varonika Rubia’s comments to heart. I love librarians. They are the smooth asphalt on a writer’s road. A research librarian is worth her or his weight in gold in my humble opinion. I wrote the following a few minutes ago and I offer it only as containing some practical experience gained through more than 30 years of being published and many experiences of soul-searing pain.
Do not just start writing text. Write an outline. In older days thesis directors and editors commonly wanted an outline, but not much now (although as to editors it may still be the case for less established writers). I have never completely followed an outline because the actual writing, additional sources, ideas, finding a weakness in reasoning and other events may not appear at first. I write a lot of law-based stuff and between the Supreme Court and Congress, I am never at a loss for needed updates. But an outline gives you a general structure and, in my case, gives me a feeling of being in control. The problem of “what next” is solved in the outline, not four chapters later. That said, don’t feel bound by the outline. A work of writing is every bit as creative as any other artistic endeavor, so expect evolution as the work begins to appear.Hopefully you will not experience the ARRRRRGHHH moment, but if you keep writing it will happen. That is the sound of a writer who just discovered a previously unknown source, someone else’s research, or just has an old-fashioned apotheosis that makes some portion of the work erroneous. It happens. Deal with it honestly. That’s what extensions of deadlines are for. Never, ever compromise on the integrity of your work. P.S. If ARRRRGHHH is followed by further screaming, however, that means an electronic failure. I am so old that my first published work was done on a state-of-the-art Selectric typewriter, when a backup copy could be either carbon paper or photocopying, but computers, hard drives, software, fails. Back up everything to a separate source, preferably a server somewhere else. Pay for the larger storage capacity of one of the major online services. I once lost a 147-page article in the final edit. Now my work is backed up to a remote server every 30 minutes because I don’t get paid more if I have to rewrite.Write some every day. There is a sort of flow to writing and thinking is more difficult to start back up when there is much of an interruption. My late husband told me that, when I was writing, he could discuss something and either just get a vacant look, or no response at all, then an hour or so later, I would answer. To me, it felt as if no time had passed. I suspect that what he said (and we are talking about the finest man to walk the earth) went into a corner of my ROM, where it stayed until there was sufficient free RAM to process it - apparently without a time stamp.Do not drink alcohol. Ever listened to a couple of drunks in a bar? Your thesis can read like they sound, or just never be finished, if you use alcohol as fuel. Eat lighter, healthy food at least once a day. My live-in caregiver is an excellent cook and as a diabetic, is big on fruits and vegetables. She puts down a plate three times a day, so I eat regularly and more healthy than I would left to myself. It does make a different. Drink juice and take vitamins. In the interest of fair disclosure, I should mention that I passed the bar on a diet of popcorn and cokes, so I am speaking here from later experience.Never mistake the first complete draft for the last one. Have your work read by another person, or read it yourself. The last edit by the writer is, for me, where the quality of the work comes together. I have literally thousands of pages in print and I am well past the stage where I think every word is golden, but on the other hand, my work is honest and readable. The embarrassing stuff has long since been edited out — for the most part by me. Never be tempted to send in that awful first go-round just to get the thing off your desk. You will be sorry, I promise.Hiring a service to write for you is, I am aware, something of a growing industry. I have never used such a service. I believe my loyal readers expect that what they read will be my work, not that of someone else. If you write a thesis or dissertation, don’t you think your professor expects that the work presented will be yours? Your professor or director or editor can make suggestions, but in the end it is your name on the page, and as a matter of scholarly integrity, it is your mind that the reader wants to see.

prompt: Write a short Python program to perform the bisection method for root finding.
text:
Sure, here's an example implementation of the bisection method in Python:

```python
def bisection(f, a, b, tol=1e-6):
    """
    Perform the bisection method to find a root of function f on the interval [a, b].
    Returns the root x and the number of iterations required.
    """
    fa, fb = f(a), f(b)
    if fa*fb > 0:
        raise ValueError("f(a) and f(b) must have opposite signs")
    x = (a + b)/2
    fx = f(x)
    n_iter = 0
    while abs(fx) > tol:
        n_iter += 1
        if fx*fa < 0:
            b = x
            fb = fx
        else:
            a = x
            fa = fx
        x = (a + b)/2
        fx = f(x)
    return x, n_iter
```

This function takes as input a function `f` (which takes a single argument), the endpoints `a` and `b` of the interval to search for a root, and an optional tolerance `tol` (defaulting to `1e-6`). It returns the root `x` found and the number of iterations required. If `f(a)` and `f(b)` have the same sign, a `ValueError` is raised.

3. Download Boot Camp Assistant. This app helps you install Windows on your Mac. You can find it in the Utilities folder in Applications.

4. Open Boot Camp Assistant. Follow the onscreen instructions to download Windows support software and create a bootable USB drive or ISO file.

5. Partition your disk to make space for Windows. Use the Boot Camp Assistant to split your disk into Windows and macOS partitions.

6. Install Windows 10. Restart your Mac and hold down the Option key to choose the Windows partition. Install Windows from the USB or ISO file.

7. Install Windows support software. Once Windows is installed, open the USB drive in File Explorer and run the setup.exe file to install drivers for your Mac hardware in Windows.

8. Set your default operating system. Use the Startup Disk tool in macOS to choose which OS you want to start up in by default. You can switch between OSes at startup by holding down the Option key.

9. Download Windows updates. Open Windows Update in the Control Panel and install all recommended updates to keep your Windows installation secure.

10. Install Windows applications. You can now install Windows apps like Microsoft Office, Adobe Creative Cloud, and more on your Mac.

prompt: Who’s more creative, Bruce Wayne or Tony Stark?
text:
Other answers to this question seem to mistake inventiveness and creativity, while there does exist some overlap, these are two different things.
 Being inventive is an act of doing. To invent something, you must have an intention to fulfill a need that is not already fulfilled by creating a new technological device. This is Tony’s wheelhouse.
The Anti-Gravity Device: A deceptively simple small red box, the Anti-Gravity Device can project an energy beam that counteracts the force of gravity for any objects inside the beam, causing them to behave as if no gravity existed. This same device can have the reverse effect — extra-gravity, increasing the force of gravity on an object — and it's powerful enough to lift entire mountains, if only for a few minutes.The Jupiter Landing Vehicle: A sturdy, versatile vehicle, the JLV was designed specifically to take on the inhospitable, heavy-gravity terrain of Jupiter. It was equipped with a sonic disrupter unit that can shatter mountains, thick treads that could navigate any terrain, lasers, and lobster-claw arms.Bleeding Edge Armor: While each armor has been impressive, the changes made for this suit are substantially more impressive, as the suit is both placed into the bones of Tony Stark to be summoned conveniently at any time, and able to self-repair via constantly replicating nano-machines.
Batman has designed the Batmobile, Batwing, Bat-boat, and all kinds of other vehicles, gadgets, and suits, but for the most part they aren’t quite in the same league as Tony’s inventions.
 Being creative however, is a state of mind. It’s how you function in the world around you. It is in your nature to come up with plans, to come up with ideas, whether it’s producing ideas for the free world, the marketplace or government, for the arts, or for yourself. Bruce Wayne would probably feel more at home here, being a genius, billionaire looking to improve his city in any way he can. On top of being a vigilante looking to cause as much fear in the hearts of criminals as possible, to the point that Amanda Waller legitimately believes that he’s a metahuman. Bruce has devised countless theoretical and posable weaknesses for a number of individuals. For example:
The Martian Manhunter's most notable weakness is fire. Batman has devised a nanite virus which, if introduced into J'onn's body, would convert the outer layer of his skin into magnesium, causing him to burst into flames upon exposure to air, a fire that wouldn’t be put out even if J’onn were to submerge himself in water.Batman has devised an altered version of Scarecrow's Fear Toxin specifically designed to cause Aquaman to become Hydrophobic, causing him to remain from any body of water and become weaker every second.Green Lantern would be rendered blind by his own power ring from a post-hypnotic suggestion introduced during the REM phase and the ring placed on him while he was asleep.When faced with Prometheus, a man with a helmet that could download skills directly into his brain, Batman replaced the martial arts skills of the 30 martial artists Prometheus had downloaded with the physical skills and coordination of Professor Stephen Hawking.
He’s pretty creative in the movies too.
 Batman Begins - Camouflage
 When Bruce has to complete his training by defeating, Ra's Al Ghul, Bruce's arm is cut. Bruce immediately considers this distinguishing injury, and then slits someone else's arm, causing Ra's to mistake another disciple for Bruce, granting Bruce a tactical advantage.
 In other words, instead of blending in with his environment, he changed his environment to blend in with him.
 Batman Forever - Coin Toss
 Batman takes advantage of his adversary's obsessive compulsion to make all his big decisions via coin toss. As the Two Face throws his coin into the air, Bruce hurls a handful of coins straight into his face, confusing the sharply dresses criminal with dozens of coins, all glittering through the air. This disrupts Two-Face's decision making process, allowing Bruce to prevail.
 The Dark Knight - Supercar Crash
 When Coleman Reese, Wayne Enterprises lawyer threatens to reveal Batman's secret identity, the Joker threatens to blow up a hospital unless someone kills him, his reason being that the revelation would ruin his fun. In order to save Reese's life while preserving his secret identity, Bruce runs a red light and crashes his sports car into Reese's convoy, causing security to tighten around Reese, preventing his untimely death.
 In addition, the idea of “The Batman” as a superhero is in and of itself a creative inversion of what superheroes were “supposed to be” at the time. While other heroes fought in the daylight, as shining beacons of hope, Batman was a symbol of terror and darkness, using fear as his primary weapon.
 The ideas themselves are what make Batman creative, not the means through which he realizes them. Tony can also be incredibly creative, but his best ideas are often the result of “eureka” moments as opposed to him actively coming up with them. (Probably not the best way to put it, but you get what I mean)
 I feel as though in terms of creativity, both are pretty even, taking into account everything they’ve been through, their ever increasing preparedness, (full on paranoia in Batman’s case) and their outlooks on life, with Batman having a slight edge, due to almost always having to outthink his opponents before he can stop them, the same happens to Tony, but on a less consistent basis, due to his tech being so formidable, But in terms of sheer inventiveness, Tony takes it. Bruce is no slouch when it comes to engineering, I mean the guy built a functioning Mother Box, but he’s no Tony Stark, Tony habitually designs new devices for solving problems that previously had no solution, Batman, while he does do the same on occasion, more often than not, elects to reverse engineer technology that he doesn't already have access to and/or or utilize what technology he does have access to in new ways, as opposed to designing new tech, unless he feels it absolutely necessary to create something completely new.

prompt: I have an ear infection. The doctor says its an otitis. Can you explain what it is?
text:
Otitis is the medical term for inflammation of the ear. There are different types of otitis depending on which part of the ear is inflamed:

• Otitis externa - This is inflammation of the outer ear, including the ear canal. It's often caused by an infection or irritation and can result in symptoms like ear pain, itchiness, drainage and hearing loss. Swimmer's ear is a common type of otitis externa. 

• Otitis media - This refers to inflammation of the middle ear, the air-filled space behind the ear drum. Otitis media is usually caused by a viral or bacterial infection and results in symptoms like ear pain, fever, hearing loss and fluid buildup in the middle ear. Acute otitis media and otitis media with effusion are two common types.

• Otitis interna - This rare type involves inflammation of the inner ear. It's often caused by viral infections that spread from the middle ear. Symptoms include vertigo, nausea, hearing loss and tinnitus.

The specific treatment for your ear infection will depend on the type of otitis you have and the cause. For bacterial otitis, antibiotics are usually prescribed. Your doctor may also recommend pain relievers, ear drops and occasionally surgery for severe or long-lasting cases. Following the treatment instructions carefully and avoiding irritants can help the otitis heal properly.

Facebook eyes Multi-Billion-$ stake in Reliance Jio for below reasons :
India is home to Facebook‘s largest user base on the planet, with hundreds of millions of people using its digital services. It now wants to get a stronger foothold in the country as more folks come online.
 Reliance Jio's presence in mobile telecom, home broadband and e-commerce will help Facebook expand its reach in the Indian digital market.
 Since launching Jio in 2016, Reliance has emerged as the only homegrown company capable of matching US tech giants in the Indian market.
 Jio, started over three years ago by multi-billionaire Mukesh Ambani, took on complacent incumbents like Airtel and Vodafone, and led the charge to make mobile data more affordable in the country. As a result, India has the cheapest data plans across the world. Now, Reliance Jio is the biggest telecom provider in the country with over 370 million subscribers.
 As per FT’s report, Facebook was “close to signing a preliminary deal for a 10 percent share,” but the deal was put off due to corona-virus outbreak. But why is the world’s biggest social network keen to invest in an Indian network telecom company? What’s in it for these companies? Let’s have a look.
 What’s in it for Facebook?
 With more than 300 million Facebook users and 400 million WhatsApp users in the country, what possible would the social media giant want? The answer is the next billion users — those who are getting on the internet for the first time in India’s developing economy.
 In 2015, Facebook introduced a program called Free Basics, which aimed to provide some apps free to users by partnering with some network providers.
 The company’s motive behind was to make Facebook a gateway to the internet for these first-time users — with the company in control of the content that people would be able to access for free. That had the potential to shape the idea of the World Wide Web for those users, while also making Facebook the most prominent brand in their online experience.
 So, by the time they graduate to the wider web, Facebook would become a major part of how they navigate the digital world. However, in 2016, India banned the Free Basics project, as it violated the country’s net neutrality rules, which dictated that all content online must be treated equally by service providers.
 With Free Basics gone, the social media giant looked to other ways of garnering traction with new internet users in India. In 2017, it launched a commercial Wi-Fi program called Express Wifi, which allows mom-and-pop stores to provide internet access to shoppers via hotspots at a nominal rate. It currently has 500 local retailers signed up, and more than 10,000 hotspots across India. It isn’t clear just how many people are using those hotspots, though.
 With Free Basics gone, the social media giant relied on some traction with its commercial WiFi program Express Wifi — that allows mom and pop stores to provide hotspots at a cheaper rate. Currently, it has 500 local entrepreneur retailers are now live with more than 10,000 hotspots across India. But there’s no detail on how many people are using those hotspots.
With Reliance Jio, the social network can start afresh and reach more people in rural areas. The network company also offers ‘smart’ feature phones, dubbed JioPhone, powered by KaiOS, that can serve apps such as YouTube, Facebook, and WhatsApp. With targeted marketing campaigns carried out by both companies, more people can use Facebook‘s set of apps.
 Another threat to Facebook is the rapid rise of Chinese apps such as TikTok and Bigo Live. Jayanth Kolla, a partner at consultancy firm Convergence Capital, noted that with slowing growth in the Indian market, Reliance Jio is the ideal partner for the social media giant to battle the Chinese onslaught:
 Reliance Jio has presented itself as a truly digital company for an average Indian. Plus, Jio‘s great at spurring a word-of-mouth marketing, so partnering with Facebook presents a great opportunity forboth of them to challenge the likes of TikTok.
 Notably, Jio has a stack of entertainment apps to woo users, including JioCinema for movies, JioTV for live TV, and JioSaavn for music streaming. However, it doesn’t operate a social network of its own yet.
 Now Let See What’s in it for Reliance Jio?
 While Reliance Jio has masterfully executed an ambitious growth strategy in India, its tech offerings haven’t really caught on. Its smartphones haven’t sold well; indigenous made-for-India projects, such as a maps service, a voice assistant, and a VR headset have all flopped.
 It has even attempted projects like a telemedicine service, and an AI-powered video call assistant. A partner with the ability to build capable and desirable technologies, like Facebook, could certainly help turn the tide for the enterprising carrier. And should Jio look to enter other markets beyond India, Facebook’s backing could make negotiations go a little easier.
 Both companies can also benefit from partnering in streaming live sports. Right now, Facebook streams live matches of the Spanish La Liga soccer league in India, while Jio has the rights to select soccer and cricket tournaments.
 In 2017, both Facebook and Jio separately put in multimillion-dollar bids to win the digital streaming rights of the Indian Premier League (IPL) cricket tournament series. While the lucrative five-year-deal went to Ruper Murdoch-owned Star Network, both internet giants could join hands to bid for these rights again in 2022.
 Conclusion
 As FT noted, Reliance Jio is valued at around $60 billion by analysts. Selling a 10 percent stake will bring Reliance closer to its goal of going debt-free by 2021.

prompt: Whas is genetic programming?
text:
Genetic programming is an evolutionary algorithm-based methodology inspired by biological evolution to find computer programs that perform a task. It works by breeding a population of computer programs using the principles of natural selection and evolution.

The basic steps in genetic programming are:

1. Define the problem and fitness function: This specifies what needs to be evolved and how to evaluate the performance of a program. The fitness function determines how "good" a program is at solving the problem.

2. Generate an initial population: This is a set of random programs created using the available building blocks (functions and terminals).

3. Evaluate each program and assign a fitness score: The fitness function is used to evaluate each program in the population and assign it a fitness score. The programs that are better at solving the problem will get a higher score.

4. Select programs to reproduce: The programs are selected to reproduce based on their fitness scores. The fitter programs get a higher chance to reproduce.

5. Breed new programs: Reproduction is done using crossover and mutation to create new programs from the selected parents.

6. Evaluate new programs and add to population: The new programs are evaluated and added to the population.

7. Repeat and evolve: Steps 3 to 6 are repeated, and over generations, the population "evolves" to get better at solving the problem.

8. Select the best program: The program with the highest fitness in the final population is selected as the solution.

Genetic programming can be used to evolve computer programs for a variety of applications like symbolic regression, image processing, game playing, etc. The key benefit is that it requires little knowledge about the domain and can often find novel solutions.

The Breton Woods agreement had been broken for more than a decade, but countries got around that by not demanding to redeem foreign currency for gold.  As for “conservatives,” I see no evidence that current politicians, Democrat or Republican, has the political will needed to balance the Federal Budget as a gold standard would require in the long run. prompt: which metrics are used to evaluate biometric systems
text:
Biometric systems are evaluated using several key performance metrics to ensure their accuracy, reliability, and efficiency. Some of the most common metrics used to evaluate biometric systems include:

1. False Acceptance Rate (FAR): The percentage of unauthorized users who are incorrectly granted access by the biometric system. A lower FAR indicates better system accuracy.

2. False Rejection Rate (FRR): The percentage of authorized users who are incorrectly denied access by the biometric system. A lower FRR indicates better system accuracy.

3. Equal Error Rate (EER): The point at which the false acceptance rate and false rejection rate are equal. A lower EER indicates better overall system performance.

4. Failure to Enroll Rate (FTER): The percentage of users who fail to enroll successfully in the biometric system, often due to poor quality data or other issues. A lower FTER indicates a more user-friendly system.

5. Failure to Capture Rate (FTCR): The percentage of times the biometric system fails to capture a biometric sample properly. A lower FTCR indicates a more reliable system.

6. Template Size: The amount of storage space required to store the biometric template for each user. Smaller template sizes are preferred for scalability and storage efficiency.

7. Matching Speed: The time it takes for the biometric system to compare a biometric sample against the stored templates and make an authentication decision. Faster matching speeds are preferred for better user experience and system efficiency.

8. System Usability: The ease of use and user-friendliness of the biometric system, which can be assessed through user feedback and surveys.

9. Robustness: The ability of the biometric system to function effectively under various environmental conditions and resist attacks or attempts to deceive the system.

10. Scalability: The ability of the biometric system to accommodate a growing number of users and handle increased demand without compromising performance.

Doob's martingale convergence theorem is a fundamental result in the theory of martingales that provides a basis for the convergence of a martingale under certain conditions. It states that if a martingale has bounded differences and is uniformly integrable, then it converges almost surely to its limit.

Let's define some terms. A martingale is a sequence of random variables that satisfies the following two properties:

1. It is adapted to the natural filtration of the underlying probability space.
2. Its expectation is constant over time.

A bounded difference martingale has the property that the absolute difference between any two consecutive terms is bounded by a constant.

Uniform integrability means that the sum of the absolute values of the expectations of the martingale is finite.

Doob's theorem states that if a martingale is both bounded difference and uniformly integrable, then it converges almost surely to its limit. This result is a key tool in the analysis of martingales and has numerous applications in probability theory and related fields.

Doob's theorem can be used to prove the martingale convergence theorems for specific types of martingales, such as the Doob-Meyer decomposition and the optional decomposition of a martingale.

prompt: What is the relationship between the average kinetic energy of electrons at two points in a circuit, and the voltage?
text:
The voltage between two points in a circuit is directly proportional to the difference in average kinetic energy of electrons between those two points.

Specifically:

Voltage = (Average Kinetic Energy at Point 2) - (Average Kinetic Energy at Point 1)

This is because voltage measures the amount of potential energy per unit charge that is gained or lost by electrons as they move through the circuit. Since kinetic energy is proportional to the square of the velocity, and the velocity of electrons increases as they move through a voltage source, their kinetic energy and hence the voltage increases.

So for example, if the average kinetic energy of electrons is 1 eV at point 1 and 3 eV at point 2, the voltage between points 1 and 2 would be 3 eV - 1 eV = 2 Volts.

The key equation is:

ΔVoltage = ΔKinetic Energy / q

Where q is the charge of an electron (1.602 x 10^-19 Coulombs)

So in short, voltage and kinetic energy are directly linked, with voltage representing the change in kinetic energy between two points, per unit charge.

Aquí hay una explicación sobre óxidos, bases y sales:

• Óxidos: Los óxidos son compuestos binarios que contienen oxígeno y otro elemento. El oxígeno tiende a tener carga negativa, mientras que el otro elemento tiene carga positiva. Los óxidos pueden ser ácidos, básicos o neutros, dependiendo de la naturaleza del otro elemento. Por ejemplo, el óxido de calcio (CaO) es una base, el óxido de dióxido de carbono (CO2) es neutro, y el óxido de dióxido de azufre (SO2) es un óxido ácido. 

• Bases: Las bases son compuestos que neutralizan los ácidos y liberan iones hidróxido (OH-) en solución acuosa. Las bases se clasifican como bases fuertes o débiles dependiendo de la fortaleza con la que liberan iones OH-. Las bases comunes incluyen hidróxidos como NaOH y KOH. Las bases reaccionan con los ácidos para formar sales y agua.

• Sales: Las sales son compuestos iónicos que se forman por la reacción de un ácido y una base. Contienen iones positivos (cationes) y negativos (aniones). Por ejemplo, cuando el ácido clorhídrico (HCl) reacciona con el hidróxido de sodio (NaOH), se forma cloruro de sodio (NaCl, sal común). Las sales son compuestos neutros que contienen iones metálicos y no metálicos. En solución acuosa, las sales se disocian en sus iones constituyentes.

En resumen, los óxidos contienen oxígeno y otro elemento, las bases liberan iones hidróxido, y las sales se forman por la reacción de ácidos y bases y contienen iones metálicos y no metálicos.

Ensuring that pulp industries pay a fair price to mango farmers involves addressing various factors and implementing effective mechanisms. Here are some considerations:

Capacity-building programs can also enhance farmers' understanding of market dynamics and improve their negotiation skills.
 5. Government regulations and interventions: Governments can play a crucial role in ensuring fair pricing for mango farmers by enacting policies and regulations that protect their interests. This can include setting minimum support prices, regulating pulp industries to prevent unfair practices, and providing subsidies or incentives to support mango cultivation.

Implementing quality standards helps ensure that farmers receive fair prices for their high-quality produce. Certifications such as organic or fair trade can provide additional value and differentiation, attracting buyers willing to pay premium prices.

Engaging in open discussions and partnerships can help foster mutually beneficial relationships, address concerns, and find solutions that promote fair pricing practices.

    reversed_sentence = " ".join(reversed_words)

1. Measurement of signal latency - The virtual machine needs to be able to accurately measure the latency (time taken) for critical signals to propagate through the system. This requires:

- Visual alerts on system monitors

prompt: Do wind turbines use diesel?
text:
In general, no. The entire point of a wind turbine is that it generates electricity by capturing some of the energy from the wind, no ‘fuel’ needed.
 But perhaps you've heard of more specialized applications, where wind turbines are used in remote locations not on the main grid. In those locations, when the wind's not blowing, the turbines aren't generating electricity. And large scale energy storage still isn't very mature, so they can’t just store excess electricity to use later. So, a lot of remote locations will use wind diesel systems. Set up a few wind turbines to generate the bulk of the electricity, and then turn on the diesel generators when the wind's not blowing. Here's an example of one such system:
[LINKED_TEXT: Hybrid wind-diesel plant meets Batan Island's total power needsThe Philippines inaugurated its first hybrid wind-diesel power plant in December. The installation, on Batan Island in the country's central Batanes province, comprises three 60 kW turbines from the French small turbine manufacturer Vergnet, and two 500 kW diesel generators. The wind turbines meet the island's total power needs from late afternoon to early morning, when the winds are at their strongest, after which the generators take over. The system is designed so that additional turbines can be added as demand increases. This is the first time Batan has had round the clock power. First Philippine Energy Corp developed the project in collaboration with Advanced Energy Systems of Australia on behalf of state-owned National Power Corps (Napocor), which also operates the plant. Napocor expects to save around PHP 2.5 million (EUR 34,000) a year in fuel costs. Energy Secretary Vincent S Perez said at the inauguration ceremony that the project was "a strong showcase of the government's commitment to renewable energy" and hoped it would be replicated elsewhere in the Philippines. "Amid the rising cost of fossil fuels," he continued, "it signals the beginning of our independence from imported oil." Vergnet says there is strong interest from public and private organizations to implement additional wind energy projects.https://www.windpowermonthly.com/article/962025/hybrid-wind-diesel-plant-meets-batan-islands-total-power-needs] [URL: https://www.windpowermonthly.com/article/962025/hybrid-wind-diesel-plant-meets-batan-islands-total-power-needs]Previously, a lot of these communities relied solely on diesel generators. The wind turbines help save them a lot on the cost of electricity by greatly reducing the amount of diesel fuel they need to import – more than enough to be worth the cost of installation. And from a tree hugger perspective, it helps reduce carbon emissions.
 On larger grids, the shear number of power plants helps make up for the shortfall when the wind's not blowing at any one wind farm. But even then, there are other sources besides wind like hydro, natural gas, and coal that can be ramped up when needed.

 Brave shuts that down and removes those delays. Here are my stats from 2 weeks of Brave :

prompt: Which paper is used for origami?
text:
Any paper you can fold; preferably square.
 The kinds of models you fold when you’re starting out (flapping bird, crane, waterbomb) will work just fine with printer paper or notebook paper. Once you learn to make a square from a rectangle, you can immediately take advantage of the near-infinite supply of discarded printouts near any printer.

That’s when you want to try the square, brightly colored paper that often comes in packs labeled ORIGAMI. (Links included at the end of this answer.) Within the origami community this material is known as ‘kami’, which (imaginatively enough) just means ‘paper’ in Japanese. This will get you an awfully long way. Almost everything you find in origami books below the super-advanced level can be folded just fine out of kami.
 Meanwhile, printer and notebook paper are still great for practice and just fooling around. I’m a lot more willing to pick up a sheet of printer paper and try out an idea, knowing that I’ll probably have to throw it away along with the next 10 variations, than I am to do the same thing to a nicer piece of paper.
 There are models that require paper with specific properties: stiffness, for example, or being exceptionally thin over a large area, or responding well to water, or being a US dollar bill. You’ll know it when you get to that stage.

Dithering is a technique used in digital imaging and audio signal processing to randomize quantization error and reduce the perception of image or audio noise. It works by adding a small amount of random data or noise to the signal being digitized, which helps to mask the effect of quantization error.

In digital imaging, dithering is often used when converting an image from a higher color depth to a lower color depth. For example, when converting a 24-bit image to 8-bit, dithering can be used to ensure that the resulting image appears more natural and less pixelated.

In audio signal processing, dithering is used to reduce the harshness that can occur when converting an analog signal to a digital signal. This is especially important when using a low-bit depth digital audio format, such as 16-bit PCM.

The basic idea behind dithering is to add a random signal that has a higher amplitude than the quantization error, but is uncorrelated with the signal being digitized. This randomization helps to spread out the quantization error, making it less perceptible to the human ear or eye.

Overall, dithering is a useful tool for improving the quality of digitized images and audio signals, and can help to ensure that the resulting output is as close as possible to the original source.

The key benefit of the OODA loop is that it allows leaders to make fast decisions in ambiguous circumstances while also adapting those decisions based on feedback and new information. prompt: What are your silly little parenting tricks that you're so glad you discovered?
text:
Here's some things that have seemed to work well with my daughter. I'll put the “silly one” first.
Hold an item in the store. I started this as soon as she was old enough to ask, a bit before 2 years old. She is always allowed to choose an item to hold while she's in the store. But she must put it back at the checkout. She gets to excitedly pore over the toys, stuffed animals and books and I get to avoid the screaming “I really really really want this!”Give choices. Always. She's in control of herself, not me. Many times the choice is between 2 things that I want her to do or even “choose to listen or choose to be disciplined”. (She did throw me a curveball with that when when it used to be choose ‘a’ discipline. She started saying, I choose to not listen and I choose time out. Lol) But for the most part it continues to work very well. It reminds her that she gets to be in control of her actions but there's a consequence to some choices.I always use the word discipline instead of punish. This is far more for me than her. It reminds me that it's never about “getting her back” for doing something that hurt or aggravated me. It's always about teaching her to become a fully functioning, well adjusted adult. It also helps me to remember some things don't need a consequence. Spilling her cereal all over herself and the floor is already upsetting. She doesn't need me to yell at her about being careless. That would not be offering her helpful guidance. That would just be letting out my frustration. So instead I let her know it's ok, it was just an accident. I know she wasn't being rambunctious or even careless. It was just an accident. Those are the moments it's most important for me to keep my cool and constantly using the word discipline reminds me of that.Everyone makes mistakes, even mommy and daddy. It's ok for her to make mistakes. We model how to deal with them by owning it when we do something wrong and apologizing and sometimes even explaining where we went wrong that led to the mistake. Then when she makes them we can help her do the same.Our daughter is actually a little bit of a perfectionist and would often not want to try for fear that she would mess up. Even after years of this “mistakes are ok” teaching. At a wonderful suggestion from a friend we began rewarding her the most for trying and not doing it perfectly. It's a load of crap that a kid can do anything if they just try. They aren't going to be great at everything. They can try and practice and practice at something and they still won't ever be great. THAT'S OK!!! There are other things they will be great at. Encourage them to try and fail. Dealing with failure is just as important as working hard and finally achieving success. I think this trick teaches them both things.I once read an article that dealt with the one phrase parents say with such anxiety. “How many times do I have to tell you this?!?” The article said that its as though there are two sides of the grand canyon. On one side is their desire to please us and the other is the desire to do what their urge wants them to. Every time you tell them what they should do it's like adding one plank in building a bridge between the 2 sides. So how many times do you have to tell them? Millions. Millions of times.Repeat key phrases of the things you really want to instill. One of the biggest ones for us is “who's always on your side? Mommy and Daddy.” When we are telling her no or disciplining or something we are doing it because we're on her side. When she's scared and we tell her we will protect her, she can trust that because we're on her side. When we're encouraging her to tell the truth, even if it will upset us she knows we will ALWAYS be on her side. When we're telling her that she was wrong and she needs to apologize she can still trust we are on her side. I'm hoping and praying that phrase sticks.It's good for your kids for you to put your marriage first. The best thing you can give your children is a healthy marriage. This is backed up by so much science and I get that for many people this is not in their control. I'm not judging. But for those of us with good partners, it's OK to tell the kids it's mommy and daddy time. Not just for the few minutes between their bedtime and yours. Not just at once a month date night. Every single day. When hubby calls on his lunch break, non urgent matters get put on hold. At night, before bedtime she has to play by herself for awhile. Yes, she gets playtime with daddy too, of course. But mommy and daddy want to talk and hang out together. Because we love each other. Kids don't always come first. My husband and I have been married for 16 years and we still just enjoy each other. We can do just fine without the other and sure, we get alone time too. But we love talking and being together. I want our kids to have that one day too. That will be so much easier if they've seen it in action. So if you have the ability to model a great relationship, don't feel guilty for doing what it takes to nurture it.Finally, don't look at your kids as extensions of yourself. Their successes are their own. Their failures are their own. It's your job to guide and nurture them. Not to do it for them. Our part as parents is monumentally important. But ultimately, none of us will ever really know how much we actually affected the outcomes. So stop taking offense when they screw up. Stop being “proud” of their achievements as though you did it just as much as they did. Be excited for them, or sad. Be impressed and enthralled with them. Be happy at every sign that shows you they are whole people, capable of succeeding on their own two feet.
That's all I've got for now.

Mass and weight are often confused, but they are quite different:

• Mass is the amount of matter in an object. It remains the same no matter where the object is.

Tensor cores:

- Optimized for AI workloads like deep learning

- CUDA cores are general purpose, Tensor cores are specialized for AI 
- CUDA cores have higher throughput, Tensor cores have lower latency 
- CUDA cores run generic CUDA programs, Tensor cores accelerate tensor operations

- You use CUDA cores for general GPU computing and machine learning training 
- You use Tensor cores to accelerate the inference phase of AI models, especially convolutional neural networks
- Having both CUDA cores and Tensor cores allows GPUs to excel at both training and inference workloads

prompt: Why is x^2 a bad activation function for a neural network?
text:
Using x^2 (square function) as an activation function for a neural network can lead to several issues, making it a poor choice. Some reasons include:

1. Non-linearity: Although the x^2 function is non-linear, it is not the most effective non-linear function for a neural network. Other functions, like sigmoid, ReLU, or tanh, provide better non-linear transformations that help the network learn complex patterns.

2. Symmetry: The square function is symmetric around the origin (0,0), which means that both positive and negative input values will produce the same output value. This can lead to difficulties in distinguishing between positive and negative input values and limit the network's ability to learn complex patterns.

3. Gradient vanishing: The derivative of the x^2 function is 2x, which means that the gradient can become very small, especially for small input values. This can lead to the vanishing gradient problem, where the network struggles to learn and update weights, particularly in deep networks.

4. Lack of sparsity: Activation functions like ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit) introduces sparsity to the activations, which can help in reducing the computation and making the network more efficient. The x^2 function does not have this property, leading to less efficient networks.

5. Monotonically increasing: The x^2 function is monotonically increasing for positive input values, which may cause the network to struggle in learning complex patterns compared to other activation functions that have a range of increasing and decreasing values (e.g., tanh).

Overall, the x^2 function is not the best choice as an activation function for a neural network due to its limitations in various aspects. Instead, more commonly used activation functions like ReLU, sigmoid or tanh should be preferred for better performance and learning capabilities.

When the government needs to borrow money to fund its operations, it issues Treasury securities, which are essentially loans from investors. The debt limit is the total amount of these securities that the government can issue and have outstanding at any given time. If the government exceeds the debt limit, it may be unable to pay its bills, including interest on existing debt, Social Security and Medicare benefits, military salaries, and other obligations.

The debt limit has been a contentious issue in American politics, with some lawmakers arguing that it is necessary to control government spending and prevent the government from incurring unsustainable levels of debt. Others argue that the debt limit is a dangerous and irresponsible tool that can lead to a default on government obligations and harm the economy.

In recent years, the debt limit has been used as a bargaining chip in negotiations over federal spending and tax policy. For example, in 2011 and 2013, the government came close to defaulting on its debt obligations because of disputes over the debt limit, prompting a last-minute agreement to raise the limit and avert a default.

text:
Here are some potential strategies to mathematically prove the Collatz conjecture:

1. Find an inductive proof. Prove that if the conjecture holds for n, it also holds for n+1. Then show it holds for the base case n=1. This would prove it for all positive integers. However, inductive proofs have been tried without success so far.

2. Find a proof by contradiction. Assume the opposite of the conjecture is true, i.e. that there exists a number n for which the sequence does not end in 1. Show that this leads to a contradiction, thereby proving the conjecture. Again, this approach has not succeeded so far. 

3. Analyze the trajectory of numbers in the Collatz sequence. Look for patterns and insights into why all trajectories end up at 1. Some properties of the trajectories are known but a full proof has not emerged. 

4. Use results from number theory. Connect the Collatz conjecture to other unsolved problems in number theory like the Goldbach conjecture or the twin prime conjecture. Solve one of these related problems first and then the Collatz conjecture may follow. This is a longshot but possible approach.

5. Perform extensive computer searches. Compute the Collatz sequences for billions of numbers and look for patterns in the data that could lead to a proof. While computers have tested up to very large numbers, an airtight proof has not yet been found this way.

6. Find a mapping between the Collatz sequence and another well-understood sequence. If the Collatz sequence could be shown to be equivalent in some way to a proven sequence, that could yield a proof. But such a mapping has not yet been found.

7. Prove a related weaker result first. Find a verifiable statement that implies the Collatz conjecture, prove that, and then the full conjecture follows. Progress on weaker results could eventually lead to a proof of the main claim.

So in summary, the main approaches are inductive proofs, proofs by contradiction, analyzing the trajectory, connecting to number theory, computer searches, mapping to other sequences, and proving weaker related results. But despite many attempts, none have succeeded yet at proving this tantalizing conjecture.

A solar inverter is a device used to convert direct current (DC) electricity from solar panels into alternating current (AC) electricity.
